---
title: "seirvax"
---

An SEIR model with hospitalisation, death and vaccination, built for
preparedness exercises. The source is on
[GitHub](https://github.com/Gulfa/modelling_prep_ex).

## The worked example

[**Influenza in Sweway**](examples/influenza.qmd) follows one outbreak from
beginning to end: a line list of a few hundred cases, the growth rate estimated
from hospital admissions, a transmission model fitted to those admissions,
checks of the age and regional patterns the fit never saw, and projections under
distancing, shielding the elderly and restricting travel between regions.

All of its data is fictional, and made for a pandemic preparedness exercise.

## Installing the package

```r
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("Gulfa/modelling_prep_ex")
```

The package is called `seirvax`; `modelling_prep_ex` is the repository. A C++
compiler is needed, since the models are compiled on installation.

## What it does

- Age groups and regions, with their contact matrices combined into one
  structure.
- A vaccinated stratum running in parallel with the unvaccinated one, with
  vaccine effectiveness against infection, transmission, hospitalisation and
  death that can vary by age.
- Hospitalisations, hospital deaths and community deaths.
- Contact multipliers and mixing matrices that change over time, for
  interventions.
- A deterministic and a stochastic version of the same model, written in
  [odin2](https://mrc-ide.github.io/odin2/) and run with
  [dust2](https://mrc-ide.github.io/dust2/).
- Fitting to daily hospital admissions with a point estimate, MCMC or particle
  MCMC, using [monty](https://mrc-ide.github.io/monty/).
- Bundled data for four fictional countries, and a generator for synthetic line
  lists to use as exercise data.
